shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.skill: Naming Shapes by Sides and Angles
shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.target: I can identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons by counting their sides and angles.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons by counting their sides and angles.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Naming shapes by how they look or how they are turned (a turned square is a “diamond”), or counting a vertex twice. Try this: Mark each side as it is counted; turn the shape and count again to see the name does not change.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.target: I can draw or choose a shape that has a given number of sides, angles, or vertices.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can draw or choose a shape that has a given number of sides, angles, or vertices.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Drawing shapes with gaps or curved sides, or thinking all quadrilaterals are squares or rectangles. Try this: Draw on dot paper with a ruler; check the number of straight sides and corners against the description.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.target: I can identify a cube and describe its 6 equal square faces, edges, and vertices.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can identify a cube and describe its 6 equal square faces, edges, and vertices.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Counting only the faces that can be seen in a picture, or calling any box a cube. Try this: Handle a real cube and mark each face with a sticker as it is counted.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.target: I can partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find how many.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find how many.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Drawing squares of different sizes, or counting some squares twice. Try this: Use square tiles first, then draw lines across and down; count by rows.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.target: I can partition circles and rectangles into 2, 3, or 4 equal shares and describe them as halves, thirds, or fourths.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.ifCorrect: You can do this: can partition circles and rectangles into 2, 3, or 4 equal shares and describe them as halves, thirds, or fourths.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Calling unequal parts halves or thirds, or thinking more parts means bigger shares. Try this: Fold paper shapes to check the shares match; compare a half and a fourth of the same strip.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-06.skill: Describing the Whole and Equal Shares
shapes-equal-shares-skill-06.target: I can describe a whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths, and explain that equal shares can have different shapes.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-06.ifCorrect: You can do this: can describe a whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths, and explain that equal shares can have different shapes.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-06.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking equal shares must look the same, or that a whole is “one half and one half” only for circles. Try this: Cut two identical squares into halves in different ways and show the pieces cover the same amount.
